page.title: Units & Calculations
page.intro: All names and personal details have been replaced with placeholders. Dates and dollar amounts are reproduced exactly as supplied. Case facts are labelled internal record: they are the requester's inputs, not official findings, and each is linked to the official rule governing that field plus a Flagged-for-Review item. Any value that would need official confirmation is left blank. {{S10}} {{S07}} {{F-19}}

sections.heading: 1. Anonymised case facts (internal record)
sections.body: Privacy control. Real names, initials, street address, APN, owner identity and contact details are not stored in this repository or published on this site. Placeholders are used throughout: Tenant A, B, C and D for Unit 1; Tenant E and F for Unit 2. SF.gov notes that Housing Inventory submissions (which contain owner/occupant information) are public — an additional reason to keep identifiers out of the site. {{S11}} {{F-19}}

sections.heading: 4. Unit 2 — illustrative sum (NOT a determination of lawful rent)
sections.body: Warning. The arithmetic below adds the seven official rates listed above. It is presented only so the numbers can be reviewed line by line. It is not a lawful-rent calculation, not a recommendation, and must not be used as the basis for a notice. Banking is fact-sensitive (24-month rule, no compounding, no rounding up, anniversary changes can permanently lose a skipped increase), the rent history is unverified, and SF.gov's own worked examples contain inconsistencies. {{S08}} {{S09}} {{S06}} {{F-07}} {{F-12}} {{F-13}} {{F-14}}

rows.item: Does a >10% combined increase change the notice period?
rows.value: Yes — 90 days' written notice under Civil Code § 827
rows.basis: "If the proposed rent increase for that tenant is greater than 10 percent … the notice shall be delivered at least 90 days before the effective date of the increase."
Cannot be confirmed: rent history, anniversary date, licence and banking eligibility are unverified. Left blank by rule.

sections.heading: 5. Conservative approach (analysis, not legal advice)
sections.body: Analysis. The lowest-scrutiny option supported by the verified sources is to forgo banked increases entirely and apply only the current published annual allowable increase (1.6% for an effective date between March 1, 2026 and February 28, 2027) to each unit on its own confirmed anniversary date, after confirming coverage and licence, with identical written notices and identical supporting documentation. This is the option most likely to be described as ordinary, formula-driven business practice. It does not guarantee that a tenant attorney would approve it — no official source can certify that. {{S01}} {{S07}} {{S11}} {{S26}} {{F-11}}

table.caption: Conservative action list — each item grounded in an official source

rows.item: Confirm coverage and licence before any notice
rows.basis: Coverage test and licence requirement.

rows.item: Use only the published annual rate
rows.basis: "For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%."

rows.item: Apply it on each tenancy's own 12-month anniversary
rows.value: No more than one increase in 12 months
rows.basis: "A landlord can impose the first annual increase 12 months after the date the tenant's lease began."

rows.item: Calculate on base rent only, no rounding up
rows.basis: "Landlords must calculate the rent increase on the tenant's base rent only." "Rent increases cannot be rounded up to the nearest dollar."

rows.item: Serve identical written notices with the same lead time and contents
rows.value: 30 days (35 by mail) for a ≤10% increase
rows.basis: Civil Code § 827 and SF Admin Code § 37.3(b).

rows.item: Do not use occupant changes or market-rent comparisons as reasons
rows.basis: § 37.3(a)(11)(A) and the six petition categories.

rows.item: Obtain written tenant-lawyer review before serving
rows.basis: Free Rent Board counseling is available but "We cannot give legal advice."
